title: 📘 UNIT 7: AFRICA SINCE 1960
notes: 🌍 Since 1960, many African countries achieved political independence through nationalist and liberation movements.

title: 7.1 🌍 RISE OF INDEPENDENT STATES IN AFRICA
notes:
🇦🇫 After the Second World War, African nationalism became stronger and colonial rule gradually declined.

🎯 Main goals of African nationalists → political independence, self-government, national unity and economic freedom.

📌 Independence was achieved through different methods, including peaceful negotiations, political movements, mass protests and armed struggle.

⭐ By the 1960s, a large number of African countries had become independent.

title: 7.1.1 🌴 NATIONAL LIBERATION IN NORTH AFRICA
notes:
🇪🇬 Egypt → the 1952 revolution ended the monarchy and strengthened Egyptian nationalism.

🇱🇾 Libya → gained independence in 1951 after the Second World War.

🇹🇳 Tunisia → achieved independence from France in 1956 under the leadership of Habib Bourguiba.

🇲🇦 Morocco → gained independence from France in 1956.

🇩🇿 Algeria → fought a major armed struggle against French colonial rule from 1954 to 1962.

🏆 Algeria gained independence in 1962 after a long and costly liberation war.

title: 7.1.2 🌴 NATIONAL LIBERATION IN WEST AFRICA
notes:
🇬🇭 Gold Coast → became Ghana in 1957 and was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule.

👤 Kwame Nkrumah → led the independence movement and promoted African unity.

🇳🇬 Nigeria → gained independence from Britain in 1960.

🇸🇳 Senegal → became independent in 1960 under the leadership of Léopold Sédar Senghor.

📌 Political parties, trade unions, educated Africans and mass movements played important roles in West African decolonization.

title: 7.1.3 🌍 NATIONAL LIBERATION IN EAST AND CENTRAL AFRICA
notes:
🇰🇪 Kenya → gained independence from Britain in 1963 after nationalist political activity and the Mau Mau struggle.

👤 Jomo Kenyatta → became Kenya's first Prime Minister and later President.

🇹🇿 Tanganyika → gained independence in 1961 under Julius Nyerere and later united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.

🇺🇬 Uganda → gained independence in 1962.

🇨🇩 Congo → gained independence from Belgium in 1960, followed by serious political instability and conflict.

📌 Central and East African liberation movements faced colonial resistance, ethnic divisions and political instability.

title: 7.1.4 🛡️ NATIONAL LIBERATION IN SOUTHERN AFRICA
notes:
🇿🇼 Zimbabwe → nationalist movements fought against white minority rule and achieved independence in 1980.

🇿🇲 Zambia → became independent from Britain in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda.

🇲🇿 Mozambique → achieved independence from Portugal in 1975 after armed struggle led by FRELIMO.

🇦🇴 Angola → gained independence from Portugal in 1975 after prolonged liberation struggle.

🇳🇦 Namibia → achieved independence in 1990 after a long struggle against South African rule.

🇿🇦 South Africa → remained under apartheid until the early 1990s.

title: 7.1.5 ⚖️ APARTHEID IN SOUTH AFRICA
notes:
⚠️ Apartheid → a system of institutionalized racial segregation and white minority rule in South Africa.

📅 1948 → the National Party formally introduced apartheid policies.

🚫 Black South Africans were denied equal political rights and faced racial segregation in residential areas, education, employment and public services.

👥 Resistance → African National Congress, Pan Africanist Congress, trade unions and other organizations fought apartheid.

👤 Nelson Mandela → became one of the most important leaders of the anti-apartheid struggle.

🌍 International pressure, sanctions and internal resistance weakened apartheid.

📅 1994 → South Africa held its first democratic multiracial election and Nelson Mandela became president.

title: 7.1.6 🤝 PAN-AFRICANISM AND THE OAU
notes:
🌍 Pan-Africanism → an ideology that promotes African unity, solidarity, freedom and cooperation.

🎯 Main ideas → oppose colonialism and racism, defend African independence and promote continental unity.

📅 May 1963 → representatives of 32 African countries met in Addis Ababa and established the Organization of African Unity.

🏛️ OAU objectives →
• Eliminate remaining colonialism and apartheid.
• Promote unity and solidarity among African states.
• Coordinate cooperation for development.
• Protect sovereignty and territorial integrity.
• Promote international cooperation.

⭐ Ethiopia played an important role in the establishment of the OAU.

title: 7.1.7 🏛️ PRINCIPAL INSTITUTIONS OF THE OAU
notes:
🏛️ Assembly of Heads of State and Government → supreme decision-making organ of the OAU.

👥 Council of Ministers → prepared matters for the Assembly and coordinated government activities.

📋 General Secretariat → administered the organization and was headed by a Secretary-General.

📌 These institutions helped member states coordinate their political and diplomatic activities.

title: 7.1.8 ⭐ SUCCESSES AND LIMITATIONS OF THE OAU
notes:
🏆 Successes → supported African liberation movements, opposed colonialism and apartheid, promoted African unity and helped settle some conflicts.

🌍 The OAU provided a common diplomatic platform for independent African states.

⚠️ Limitations → respect for state sovereignty sometimes restricted intervention in internal conflicts.

⚠️ Other problems → limited financial resources, political disagreements, military coups, civil wars and economic dependence.

📌 Despite its limitations, the OAU laid the foundation for greater continental cooperation.

title: 7.2 💰 STRUGGLE FOR ECONOMIC INDEPENDENCE
notes:
💰 Political independence did not automatically bring economic independence.

🌍 Many African economies remained dependent on former colonial powers and foreign companies.

📦 Major problem → economies often depended heavily on exporting a few primary commodities while importing manufactured goods.

⚠️ Consequences → vulnerability to world market prices, foreign debt, unemployment and slow industrial development.

🎯 African countries therefore sought economic cooperation, industrialization, diversification and greater control over natural resources.

title: 7.2.1 🌍 REGIONAL ECONOMIC INTEGRATION
notes:
🤝 Regional Economic Communities were created to strengthen cooperation and economic integration among African countries.

🎯 Main purposes → increase trade, coordinate development, improve infrastructure and strengthen collective bargaining power.

📜 Lagos Plan of Action → adopted in 1980 and emphasized African self-reliance and economic development.

📜 Abuja Treaty → signed in 1991 and provided a framework for establishing an African Economic Community.

📌 Regional integration became an important strategy for overcoming economic dependence.

title: 7.2.2 🌐 MAJOR REGIONAL ECONOMIC COMMUNITIES
notes:
🌍 COMESA → Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa; established in 1994 and promoted regional trade and economic integration.

🌍 ECOWAS → Economic Community of West African States; promotes economic cooperation and regional integration in West Africa.

🌍 IGAD → Intergovernmental Authority on Development; promotes cooperation and development in the Horn of Africa.

🌍 SADC → Southern African Development Community; promotes regional development and economic cooperation in Southern Africa.

⭐ These organizations support trade, development, peace and regional cooperation.

title: 7.3 🌍 MAJOR ISSUES IN CONTEMPORARY AFRICA
notes:
⚠️ African countries have faced major political, economic, social and environmental challenges since independence.

📌 Major issues include → poverty, unemployment, rapid population growth, ethnic conflicts, political instability, civil wars, disease, environmental degradation and climate-related problems.

💰 Economic challenges → dependence on primary commodities, foreign debt, limited industrialization and unequal development.

🏛️ Political challenges → military coups, weak institutions, corruption, authoritarianism and conflict.

🌱 Environmental challenges → drought, desertification, deforestation, soil degradation and water scarcity.

title: 7.3.1 👥 POPULATION, POVERTY AND UNEMPLOYMENT
notes:
👥 Rapid population growth → increases pressure on land, food, housing, education, health services and employment.

💰 Poverty → remains a major development challenge in many African countries.

👷 Unemployment → particularly affects young people and contributes to migration and social problems.

📌 Solutions require investment in education, health, agriculture, industry, infrastructure and employment opportunities.

title: 7.3.2 ⚔️ ETHNIC CONFLICTS AND POLITICAL INSTABILITY
notes:
⚠️ Ethnic conflicts → competition over political power, land, resources and representation can produce violent conflict.

🪖 Military coups → occurred in several African countries after independence and often interrupted constitutional government.

⚔️ Civil wars → caused deaths, displacement, destruction of infrastructure and economic decline.

🕊️ Peacebuilding → requires inclusive political institutions, dialogue, good governance and respect for human rights.

title: 7.3.3 🦠 HEALTH AND SOCIAL CHALLENGES
notes:
🏥 African countries have faced major public health challenges, including HIV/AIDS and other infectious diseases.

📌 Limited healthcare facilities, poverty, inadequate sanitation and shortages of trained health workers can worsen these problems.

🎓 Education and healthcare investment → essential for improving human development and reducing poverty.

🤝 International and regional cooperation → important in addressing major health challenges.

title: 7.3.4 🌱 ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLIMATE CHALLENGES
notes:
🌍 Major environmental problems → drought, desertification, deforestation, soil erosion and water shortages.

🌡️ Climate change → increases the risks of droughts, floods and food insecurity.

🌾 Effects → reduced agricultural production, displacement and increased competition over natural resources.

🎯 Sustainable development → requires environmental protection, improved agricultural practices, water management and regional cooperation.

title: 🏆 UNIT 7 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
🌍 AFRICAN INDEPENDENCE

1957 → Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence.

1960 → known as the "Year of Africa" because many African countries gained independence.

1962 → Algeria gained independence after a major war against France.

1963 → Kenya became independent and the OAU was established in Addis Ababa.

1975 → Angola and Mozambique gained independence from Portugal.

1990 → Namibia gained independence.

1994 → South Africa held its first democratic multiracial election.

🤝 PAN-AFRICANISM AND OAU

Pan-Africanism → promoted African unity, freedom and solidarity.

OAU → established in Addis Ababa in May 1963 by 32 African countries.

Main objectives → eliminate colonialism and apartheid, promote unity, protect sovereignty and coordinate development.

💰 ECONOMIC INDEPENDENCE

Political independence did not end economic dependence.

Major problems → dependence on primary commodities, foreign debt, unemployment and limited industrialization.

Regional cooperation → COMESA, ECOWAS, IGAD and SADC promoted economic integration.

🌍 CONTEMPORARY AFRICA

Major challenges → poverty, unemployment, population pressure, ethnic conflicts, political instability, disease, environmental degradation and climate change.

🧠 BIG PICTURE → African nationalism led to political independence across the continent. However, independence did not immediately solve economic and social problems. African countries established the OAU to promote unity and defend sovereignty, while regional economic organizations encouraged cooperation and development. Despite major achievements, Africa continues to face challenges involving poverty, conflict, unemployment, population growth, health and environmental change.
